entries.clue: Affection simulated by AI strangely irks sceptics at first (3,4)

indicatorNotes.strangely: IRKS behaving strangely is IRKS rearranged
indicatorNotes.at first: takes only the opening letter of sceptics

annotation.surface: Sceptics bristle at a chatbot faking tenderness.
annotation.walkthrough: An air kiss is affection only in pretence, a kiss blown near the cheek, so 'simulated' belongs in the definition rather than the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: An air kiss mimics a kiss without contact, a show of affection that is not quite real.

entries.clue: Handshake perhaps is one welcome when introducing people (9)

indicatorNotes.when introducing: one welcome introduces MEN into itself, taking them inside

annotation.surface: A handshake as the polite greeting when strangers are introduced.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Introducing' looks like a social introduction but is the instruction to insert. 'Perhaps' marks a handshake as one example of sealing an agreement.
annotation.definitionFit: A handshake is the traditional way of sealing an agreement.

entries.clue: Chilling pair at heart of horror (1,3,1)

indicatorNotes.at heart of: the heart of a word is its central letters

blocks.note: the first of the two central letters of the six-letter word
a pair is one thing plus another, so the two central letters are spoken with a joining word between them
the second of the two central letters

annotation.surface: A pair of spine-chilling moments at the centre of a horror film.
annotation.walkthrough: The central two letters of horror are R and R, read out as a phrase. 'Chilling' looks like fear but is slang for relaxing, and R and R is rest and recreation.
annotation.definitionFit: R and R (rest and recreation) is time spent chilling out.

entries.clue: Vehicles essentially picking up diver in danger at sea (7)

indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence of vehicles is its middle
indicatorNotes.picking up: in a down clue, picking up lifts GREBE so it reads upward

blocks.note: the middle two letters of vehICles
the grebe is a diving bird

annotation.surface: Rescue vehicles collecting a diver in trouble offshore.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Diver' pictures a person in a wetsuit; it is the grebe, a diving water bird.
annotation.definitionFit: Icebergs are a classic hazard to shipping.

entries.clue: Beginning to scratch bum cheek (4)

indicatorNotes.Beginning to: takes the opening letter of scratch

annotation.surface: Someone starting to scratch their backside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cheek' continues the bottom joke, but it means impudence here. Bum is British slang for the backside.
annotation.definitionFit: Sass is impudent back-talk, which is cheek.

entries.clue: Dance with retired doctor showing lack of coordination (7)

indicatorNotes.retired: something retired has gone back, so DR runs backwards

annotation.surface: A retired doctor clumsily dancing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retired' looks like the doctor's career status; it is the instruction to turn DR round.
annotation.definitionFit: Discord is disharmony, a failure to work together.

entries.clue: Notice group cutting venison for spit (4,6)

indicatorNotes.cutting: AD and RING cut into DEER, sitting inside it

blocks.note: a ring is a group, as in a spy ring

annotation.surface: A notice about carving venison for roasting on a spit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spit' suggests a roasting skewer; it is the 'dead spit' of someone, an exact likeness.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who is the spit of another, the spitting image, is a dead ringer for them.

entries.clue: Legendary one saved squirrels (7)

indicatorNotes.saved: STORED keeps the I inside it, as if saved

blocks.note: to squirrel something away is to store it

annotation.surface: A famous squirrel that once rescued someone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Squirrels' reads as a plural noun but is a verb, squirrels away, meaning stored.
annotation.definitionFit: A storied place or person is celebrated in stories, which is legendary.

entries.clue: Spotted in lover's pendant, go red? (9)

indicatorNotes.Spotted in: the answer can be spotted inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: A blush noticed on a gift pendant from a lover.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Go red' suggests blushing; here it is going into the red, the colour of debt in a bank statement.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: going red, or into the red, means your account is overdrawn, the result of spending more than you have.

entries.clue: Plan of road heading uphill and back (5)

indicatorNotes.heading uphill: in a down clue, heading uphill makes RD read from bottom to top

blocks.note: aft = at the back of a ship

annotation.surface: A plan of a road climbing a hill and returning.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a route description; 'and back' is a separate piece, AFT, not part of the return trip.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a draft is the rough first version of a document or design, drawn up before the final one.

entries.clue: Field buzzed with energy (5)

blocks.note: a doorbell or phone that buzzed rang

annotation.surface: A meadow humming with energetic insects.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Field' pictures grass; here it is a field of expertise, a range.
annotation.definitionFit: A range is a scope or sphere, as a field of study is.

entries.clue: Rise to embrace bishop with a melodramatic show (4,5)

indicatorNotes.to embrace: SOAR wraps its arms around POPE

blocks.note: the Pope is the Bishop of Rome

annotation.surface: A dramatic moment where someone rises to hug a bishop.
annotation.walkthrough: SOA(POPE)R, then A. 'Bishop' is often B or RR in crosswords; here it is the Pope, Bishop of Rome.
annotation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a serial drama known for melodrama.

entries.clue: Student leaving out cap means to collect money (6)

indicatorNotes.leaving out cap: the cap of a word is its first letter, here dropped

blocks.note: a learner is a student, as on the L-plates of a British learner driver
the cap is the top of the word, its first letter, and it is the one that goes

annotation.surface: A student going without a hat to raise funds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cap' looks like a hat; it is the top letter of the word. A nice little earner is British slang for a profitable sideline.
annotation.definitionFit: An earner is a source of income, a way of making money.

entries.clue: Model recalled art teacher's education (5,3)

indicatorNotes.recalled: called back, so ART runs backwards

blocks.note: INSET is in-service training for teachers

annotation.surface: A sitter remembering an art teacher's training.
annotation.walkthrough: In British schools an INSET day is a staff training day with no pupils. 'Model' looks like an artist's sitter but describes a model railway.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a train set is a toy railway built to scale, one kind of model.

entries.clue: Beef dish got mixed with saffron (10)

indicatorNotes.mixed: ingredients that are mixed are stirred together, so the letters lose their order

annotation.surface: A beef dish flavoured with saffron.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a recipe note, so 'mixed' passes for a cooking step rather than an instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Beef stroganoff is a Russian dish of beef strips in sour cream sauce.

entries.clue: Woke in the end with leg broken (11)

indicatorNotes.broken: the letters are broken up and reassembled

annotation.surface: Someone waking up at last with a broken leg.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Woke' reads as the past tense of wake; it is the adjective meaning alert to injustice.
annotation.definitionFit: Woke means socially aware, enlightened about injustice.

entries.clue: Despicable look at last of burglars breaking in (9)

indicatorNotes.last of: takes the final letter of burglars
indicatorNotes.breaking: S breaks into HOME, like a burglar

blocks.note: lo = look, as in lo and behold

annotation.surface: A despicable glimpse of the last burglar breaking into a house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Breaking in' is split: 'breaking' is the instruction and 'in' is HOME, as in staying in.
annotation.definitionFit: Loathsome means hateful, deserving contempt.

entries.clue: English bachelors head out (3)

blocks.note: B = bachelor, doubled for the plural

annotation.surface: English bachelors setting off somewhere.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head out' is what the tide does as it ebbs, not a group leaving.
annotation.definitionFit: When the tide ebbs it flows out.

entries.clue: Series of shuttle launches got through terrible moment, not taking off (9)

indicatorNotes.taking off: in a down clue, taking off means rising, so NOT reads upwards

annotation.surface: Space shuttles repeatedly failing to lift off at a tense moment.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about space launches; the shuttle is a shuttlecock, hit back and forth over a net.
annotation.definitionFit: Badminton is played by launching a shuttlecock to and fro.

entries.clue: Endless source of milk for hot drink (3)

indicatorNotes.Endless: the word loses its end letter

blocks.note: a teat is where milk comes from

annotation.surface: A constant supply of milk for a cuppa.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Endless' suggests a supply that never runs out; it cuts off the final letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym by example: tea is the hot drink milk most often goes into in Britain.

entries.clue: Complicated ode, abridged and broken down (11)

indicatorNotes.Complicated: the letters are put in a complicated order

annotation.surface: A difficult poem that has been cut and fallen apart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Abridged' looks like an instruction to shorten, but it is just fodder letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Something biodegraded has been broken down by natural processes.

entries.clue: Foundation degree in education and music (7)

blocks.note: rock is a kind of music

annotation.surface: A foundation course in teaching and music.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Foundation degree' reads as a British qualification, but the split falls between them.
annotation.definitionFit: Bedrock is the fundamental basis of something.

entries.clue: Priest offers shelter to accident's first responder (7)

indicatorNotes.first: takes the opening letter of accident

blocks.note: a rector is a parish priest

annotation.surface: A priest giving shelter to the first person on the scene of an accident.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First responder' is a paramedic phrase; the split falls after 'first', leaving 'responder' alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A reactor is one who reacts, or responds.

entries.clue: Start to eat deconstructed sandwich wife's left in layers (8)

indicatorNotes.Start to: takes the opening letter of eat
indicatorNotes.deconstructed: the sandwich is taken apart and rebuilt
indicatorNotes.left: the wife's W is left out of the fodder

annotation.surface: Someone starting a deconstructed sandwich while a wife is left in layers of clothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Layers' sounds like strata; it means egg-layers, since the echidna is one of the few mammals that lays eggs.
annotation.definitionFit: Echidnas are egg-laying mammals, so they are layers.

entries.clue: Displays latex posing pouches (5)

indicatorNotes.pouches: the phrase pouches the answer, holding it inside

annotation.surface: A display of people posing in latex.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pouches' reads as a noun; it is a verb, holding the answer within.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: expo is short for exposition, a trade fair where goods are put on display.

entries.clue: Farewell note for Mat (6)

blocks.note: mi, the third note of the scale

annotation.surface: A goodbye note left for someone called Mat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mat' has a capital to pass as a name; it is a tatami, a Japanese straw floor mat.
annotation.definitionFit: A tatami is a traditional Japanese floor mat.

entries.clue: Friend and I leave after mum comes around (5)

indicatorNotes.comes around: MA turns round to read AM
indicatorNotes.after: 'leave after' puts GO later in the word than what precedes it, so the reversed MA and I come first

annotation.surface: A friend and I head off once mum turns up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Comes around' reads as mum visiting; it turns MA the other way.
annotation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, used informally in English.

entries.clue: Maybe sister and I pulled up waders (4)

indicatorNotes.pulled up: in a down clue, pulled up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a sister is one kind of sibling, a sib

annotation.surface: A sister and I hauling up our fishing waders.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Waders' suggests rubber boots; it means wading birds. The plural fits because ibis can be its own plural.
annotation.definitionFit: Ibises are long-legged wading birds.

entries.clue: Discreetly get shot of Asian food smell in burial chamber (9)

indicatorNotes.in: a smell in a chamber is inside it, so the smell's letters go within the chamber's

blocks.note: pho is a Vietnamese noodle soup
a tomb is a burial chamber

annotation.surface: Quietly getting rid of smelly Asian food in a burial chamber.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get shot of' is British for get rid of, but here it means sneaking into a shot, a photo.
annotation.definitionFit: To photobomb is to slip unnoticed into someone else's photo.

entries.clue: Charlie secures head of screwdriver in screw (5)

indicatorNotes.head of: takes the first letter of screwdriver

blocks.note: a charlie is a fool, a twit

annotation.surface: A man called Charlie fitting a screwdriver bit into a screw.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' looks like a name; in British slang a charlie is a fool.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: you drive a screw home by turning it, so to screw and to twist are the same motion.

entries.clue: Discuss loudly after very engaging summit (5,2)

indicatorNotes.engaging: SO engages PEAK, holding it inside
indicatorNotes.after: 'loudly after' places the loud letter behind everything else, at the end of the answer

annotation.surface: Talking loudly after a very engaging summit meeting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Summit' suggests a diplomatic meeting; it is a mountain peak.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the phrasal verb means to mention or talk about a subject, as in 'speaking of which'.

entries.clue: Knight, courageous one, experiencing change of heart gets cut (7)

indicatorNotes.experiencing change of heart: the middle letters of LION change places

annotation.surface: A brave knight who has a change of heart and gets hurt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut' reads as a wound; it is a cut of beef.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the butcher's sense of cut, a joint of meat, and sirloin is one taken from the upper loin of beef.
